director.chapterArc: Traumatic counting and physical diagnosis settle into a logistics crisis; Katori sacrifices the hidden cargo to preserve the mother, Callie learns to define both her moral and supernatural limits, and the company reaches Meridian with a brief recovery of dignity. The arrival then reverses into forensic threat-reading: a Barrel has been killed, harvested, and buried beside a named mule. End on Pell converting grief back into duty.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder measured and observational. Let grief register through numbers, stillness, touch, and practical decisions—not vocal collapse. Keep tactical debate and track-reading neutral and spatially exact. The few humorous lines are dry pressure releases. Treat the Barrel as evidence rather than spectacle, and make PITCH land as a humanizing fact rather than a horror reveal.

cues.delivery: Let the stopped count and the unreturned gaze carry the loss; remain almost reportorial, with no tremor or elegiac weight.
cues.from: It stopped at a hundred and fifty-eight.
cues.through: She did not say anything. Her eyes were open and they were looking at the canvas, and they did not come round to Callie's face.
cues.reason: The chapter opens inside Callie's mechanical processing of presumed death.

cues.delivery: Physically weakened and effortful, each broken piece testing whether speech still works; avoid a performed stutter.
cues.from: "Cal," she said. It was thick and slow and wrong at the edges. "Cal. Lie."
cues.through: "Cal," she said. It was thick and slow and wrong at the edges. "Cal. Lie."
cues.reason: The mother's damaged recognition is the first reversal from apparent death.

cues.delivery: Dry self-assessment offered as permission to survive the indignity; do not solicit a laugh.
cues.from: "Well," she said at last. "That's new."
cues.through: "Well," she said at last. "That's new."
cues.reason: The mother uses wit to regain a small measure of authority.

cues.delivery: Keep the joke practical and unsentimental, then make the field metaphor a precise description of bodily disobedience.
cues.from: "It's all right," said her mother. "You're allowed to. I'd laugh if it was anybody else." She looked down the length of herself at the leg under the blanket. "I can feel it. I just can't tell it anything. It's like shouting at somebody in the next field."
cues.through: "It's all right," said her mother. "You're allowed to. I'd laugh if it was anybody else." She looked down the length of herself at the leg under the blanket. "I can feel it. I just can't tell it anything. It's like shouting at somebody in the next field."
cues.reason: Humor masks the frightening permanence of the paralysis.

cues.delivery: Pell protects Duchess by stating her limits as fact; the final verdict should be quiet, immovable, and free of sentimentality.
cues.from: "She'll walk," Pell said. He did not turn round. "She'll walk because she's a horse and a horse will walk on anything short of a broken leg, and it's not broken. I'd know." He was quiet. "She won't pull."
cues.through: "She'll walk," Pell said. He did not turn round. "She'll walk because she's a horse and a horse will walk on anything short of a broken leg, and it's not broken. I'd know." He was quiet. "She won't pull."
cues.reason: His affection appears as refusal to exploit the injured horse.

cues.delivery: A private acknowledgment of what abandoning the crates costs Katori; keep it contained entirely in the held hand and lowered head.
cues.from: Katori put her hand flat on the top of the nearest one. She held it there. Her head went down.
cues.through: Katori put her hand flat on the top of the nearest one. She held it there. Her head went down.
cues.reason: This is the silent point at which Katori accepts the sacrifice.

cues.delivery: Deliver the plan as settled logistics; allow only the last two short sentences to reveal that a life has outranked the promise.
cues.from: "Then we'll take them to the bridge," said Katori, "and we'll put them under the north pier, where it's dry. And we'll mark it in the book. And we'll go on without them, and we'll come back for them." She took her hand off the crate. "They'll keep. She won't."
cues.through: "Then we'll take them to the bridge," said Katori, "and we'll put them under the north pier, where it's dry. And we'll mark it in the book. And we'll go on without them, and we'll come back for them." She took her hand off the crate. "They'll keep. She won't."
cues.reason: Katori chooses the mother over the concealed burden.

cues.delivery: A nearly suppressed release of pressure: affectionate accusation, with gratitude left unspoken.
cues.from: "Correct of her," said Katori, reading it, and something moved at the corner of her mouth. "Pell, you old fraud."
cues.through: "Correct of her," said Katori, reading it, and something moved at the corner of her mouth. "Pell, you old fraud."
cues.reason: Pell's record validates Callie's refusal while giving the group a dry moment of relief.

cues.delivery: The mother claims dignity without pleading; warmth belongs to her gratitude for being carried, firmness to the choice she reserves for herself.
cues.from: "I want one." Her mother did not lift the hat off her eyes. "Not now. At the gate. The morning we get there. I've been thinking about it since the hill." She was quiet. "I'm not going in through that gate on my back. I've been carried a long way by a great many people who had other things to do, and I've let them, and I'll let them again. But not through the gate. I want to walk in. On my own two feet. I want them to see me walk in."
cues.through: "I want one." Her mother did not lift the hat off her eyes. "Not now. At the gate. The morning we get there. I've been thinking about it since the hill." She was quiet. "I'm not going in through that gate on my back. I've been carried a long way by a great many people who had other things to do, and I've let them, and I'll let them again. But not through the gate. I want to walk in. On my own two feet. I want them to see me walk in."
cues.reason: She defines why walking through the gate matters.

cues.delivery: Firm maternal authority, not irritation: she knows the cost and calmly establishes whose cost it is to spend.
cues.from: "I know what it'll cost me. I was there." Her mother lifted the hat at last and looked at her. "It's mine to spend. We settled that at the bottom of the scarp. The other three are yours. I'm not going to argue about the other three."
cues.through: "I know what it'll cost me. I was there." Her mother lifted the hat at last and looked at her. "It's mine to spend. We settled that at the bottom of the scarp. The other three are yours. I'm not going to argue about the other three."
cues.reason: The mother reasserts agency over her medicine and body.

cues.delivery: Protective foresight spoken evenly; the prohibition must land as a safeguard against Callie's reflex to sacrifice everything, not as a farewell speech.
cues.from: "When we get there, you're going to want to sign things." She said it very evenly. "You're going to stand in front of whoever's got the book, and they're going to tell you what it costs, whatever it is. And you're going to say yes to all of it before they've finished the sentence, because it's me. I know you. I've known you since you had your head stuck in the elevator rails." She was quiet for a moment. "Don't. Not without me. Whatever it is. Whatever they say. You don't sign one thing for me without me there to hear it."
cues.through: "When we get there, you're going to want to sign things." She said it very evenly. "You're going to stand in front of whoever's got the book, and they're going to tell you what it costs, whatever it is. And you're going to say yes to all of it before they've finished the sentence, because it's me. I know you. I've known you since you had your head stuck in the elevator rails." She was quiet for a moment. "Don't. Not without me. Whatever it is. Whatever they say. You don't sign one thing for me without me there to hear it."
cues.reason: The mother anticipates the moral danger of admission paperwork.

cues.delivery: Ines inventories hard-won skill without pride; soften only on the mother's teaching method, where respect replaces praise.
cues.from: "I'm not good at it. I was good at dresses. I had to get good at people on this road because nobody else was going to." Ines put the scissors away. "Your mother taught me more about it in one night in a pump house than I'd learned in eleven years." She was quiet for a moment, with the kit in her lap. "She's a good teacher. She doesn't tell you you're doing it right. She just tells you smaller until you are."
cues.through: "I'm not good at it. I was good at dresses. I had to get good at people on this road because nobody else was going to." Ines put the scissors away. "Your mother taught me more about it in one night in a pump house than I'd learned in eleven years." She was quiet for a moment, with the kit in her lap. "She's a good teacher. She doesn't tell you you're doing it right. She just tells you smaller until you are."
cues.reason: The road's brutality briefly resolves into gratitude for transmitted competence.

cues.delivery: Turn inward around the unrecorded word; hold it as borrowed trust, then settle the decision to withhold it without secrecy-for-effect.
cues.from: Then she thought of the thing that was not in there. The word.
cues.through: She would leave it out. That was the one thing she would leave out. Not because it was a lie, but because it was not hers to give them.
cues.reason: Callie identifies the one truth that is not hers to surrender.

cues.delivery: Pell speaks to himself as he distinguishes policy from failure; give 'decision' the chill of deliberate human control.
cues.from: "It's a decision," said Pell, somewhere under the wagon. He said it very quietly, to himself. "It's not broken. It's a decision."
cues.through: "It's a decision," said Pell, somewhere under the wagon. He said it very quietly, to himself. "It's not broken. It's a decision."
cues.reason: The extinguished bank lights become evidence of an unknown authority.

cues.delivery: A small, private greeting to a returned part of the body; wonder contained inside familiar recognition.
cues.from: "Oh," said her mother. "There you are."
cues.through: "Oh," said her mother. "There you are."
cues.reason: The mother's leg answers her for the first time.

cues.delivery: Call for Ines without taking attention off the evidence; quiet because Callie already understands the scale of what she has found.
cues.from: "Ines," said Callie. Her voice came out very quiet.
cues.through: "Ines," said Callie. Her voice came out very quiet.
cues.reason: The human-sized hollow changes the track-reading into immediate danger.

cues.delivery: Pell supplies the name like a rare measurement; let the survival fact lower the temperature rather than enlarging the monster.
cues.from: "There's a word," said Pell, from the board. He had not got down. He was looking at the bent rail. "I've heard it said twice in my life. A Barrel." He was quiet. "I never met anybody who'd seen one and was still standing up."
cues.through: "There's a word," said Pell, from the board. He had not got down. He was looking at the bent rail. "I've heard it said twice in my life. A Barrel." He was quiet. "I never met anybody who'd seen one and was still standing up."
cues.reason: Naming the Barrel establishes the threat's exceptional scale.

cues.delivery: Bone-dry understatement from a woman reading catastrophe as another difficult day's work.
cues.from: "Well," she said. "Someone's had a day."
cues.through: "Well," she said. "Someone's had a day."
cues.reason: The mother punctures the group's stunned silence without reducing the danger.

cues.delivery: Keep Pell perfectly level; the grief lies in recognizing that the buried animal was known, not in displaying sorrow.
cues.from: "Somebody named it," Pell said at last.
cues.through: His voice was perfectly level. It was the voice he used for distances. It did not go up at the end.
cues.reason: The painted name turns physical evidence into a personal loss.

cues.delivery: Treat the hand on the board as a brief acknowledgment owed to a working animal; no lingering sentiment, only respect completed through touch.
cues.from: He stood there a moment longer. Then he put out his hand and laid it flat on the top of the board, the way he had laid it on Duchess's leg at first light, and held it there, and took it away.
cues.through: He stood there a moment longer. Then he put out his hand and laid it flat on the top of the board, the way he had laid it on Duchess's leg at first light, and held it there, and took it away.
cues.reason: Pell silently records PITCH before returning the company to duty.
